name: Vector_Basis_1
questiontext:
Given is a spanning set \(S\) of a subspace \(U \subset R^4\):

\[ S = \{ {{CT:0}},\ {{CT:1}},\ {{CT:2}},\ {{CT:3}},\ {{CT:4}} \}. \]

Find a basis of \(U\).

Enter the vectors in the basis as rows in the matrix below, adding zero rows (at the bottom!) when there are less than 5 vectors in the basis.

[[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

How to enter: each entry in its own box: a number, a fraction (e.g. 1/2) or an expression (e.g. sqrt(2)).
generalfeedback:
A basis is most easily found by using the vectors in the spanning set as the rows in a matrix:

\[ {{CT:5}}. \]

The subspace spanned by them is then the same as the rowspace of this matrix. Reduction to Echelon form will then reveal both the rank (dimension of the subspace) and a basis (the non-zero rows). An Echelon form of the matrix above is

\[ {{CT:6}}.\]

A basis is then given by the non-zero rows:

\[ {{CT:7}}.\]

(Reminder: any \({{CT:8}}\) linear independent vectors that can be written as a combination of the given vectors will form a basis.)

prts.name: Result

on_true.feedback: You have the right number of linearly independent vectors.

on_false.feedback: You do not have the right number of linearly independent vectors.

on_true.feedback: You do not have the right number of linearly independent vectors.

on_false.feedback: You do not have the right number of linearly independent vectors.

on_true.feedback: All your non-zero vectors are in the given subspace.

on_false.feedback: Some of your non-zero vectors are not in the given subspace.
